data.name: Aryesh
data.gender_notes: Aryesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit words ‘arya’ (noble) and ‘ish’ (lord, master). This name signifies a noble and courageous leader. The name Aryesh carries the meaning “Noble, Courageous One” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Aryesh usually hope their child will grow to embody noble, courageous one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of inner wisdom and strength.
data.etymology: Aryesh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Noble, Courageous One.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aryesh total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.reference: The name Aryesh is believed to be derived from the Sanskrit word 'Arya' meaning 'noble' or 'pure' and the Persian suffix '-esh' meaning 'lord' or 'ruler'. This name was commonly used among the Aryan people of ancient India around 1500 BCE.

Aryesh is also mentioned in the Hindu epic 'Mahabharata' as the name of a great warrior from the Kuru kingdom who fought in the epic battle of Kurukshetra. His father was Bhishma, the grandsire of the Pandavas and the Kauravas.
